identity: Civil rights advocate and writer · United States · 1929–1968
title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s birth chart
metaDescription: Martin Luther King Jr.'s chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.1° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mutable signs carry five of the ten placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. The mutable signs hand one season to the next; a chart weighted there is built for transitions.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Capricorn, but precisely: 25.1°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Mercury in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 11.7° Aquarius, Venus was at 10.5° Pisces, Mars was at 21.9° Gemini. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Jupiter to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.3°. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Mars opposition Saturn at 3.4°, and Saturn trine Neptune at 5.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune close a triangle of trines. The closed triangle is the scheme’s picture of flow — and its warning that flow, unspent, stays private. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has one entry for this chart. Venus in Pisces at 10.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: earth 3, water 3, air 2, fire 2 across the elements, and mutable 5, cardinal 3, fixed 2 across the modalities. Mars, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 19.1°.
